correctness.rationale: With duplicate deletion histories collapsed, a two-output word has an adjacent repeated pair and uses exactly one diagonal receiver. Constants also use one diagonal receiver. Thus A+B≤2q and A≤q for the one- and two-output strata, and the complete receiver incidence count E≤2q², giving 3|C|=E+(A+B)+A≤2q²+3q. An independent receiver-side exhaustive insertion check reproduced (q, size, E, number of list-one receivers, number of list-two receivers) = (4,14,30,2,14), (5,21,48,2,23), (6,30,72,0,36), (8,50,126,2,62), with no empty or overfull receivers. The six-symbol equality conditions and its cyclic construction check out; a three-output word with a diagonal output cannot occur in an equality case because constants and two-output words exhaust the diagonal capacity. The two displayed conflict triangles have distinct edge witnesses (20,24,23) and (43,63,03), and the cyclic action is free, so the nondivisibility arguments apply to all optima of the other three sizes. The enumeration is over receivers of the exhibited codes only, not over all codebooks; the general bound provides optimality.
residual_risks: The certificate gives no existence claims at other alphabet sizes or nondecomposability of all five- or eight-symbol optima.

value.rationale: The four sizes are motivated first representatives beyond the usual Steiner classes, not an arbitrary sample. The universal upper bound cannot decide sharpness there. Concrete saturation, symmetry and odd-cycle witnesses distinguish genuine list-two packing from simply combining unique codes and give reusable test cases for future general constructions.
residual_risks: Finite case result; no general non-Steiner existence or rigidity theorem is established.
